knowledge_gaps: The recurrence h=z*r*h_previous+(1-z)*candidate is not ordinary GRU interpolation: its coefficients sum to 1-z*(1-r), which can shrink state magnitude without increasing the candidate contribution. Improvements could reflect shrinkage rather than useful selective forgetting.

The item-only gate assigns the same retention to an item across histories in evaluation mode. Its ability to distinguish repeated coherent behavior from isolated interests is therefore limited; contextual adaptation remains in the ordinary GRU gates.
The implementation notes contradict themselves by first adding gates to every layer and then specifying only the first layer. Declare first-layer-only gating consistently.

The supplied module does not implement train.py, the predictor writer, diagnostic integration or an explicit checkpoint-selection rule. Reproducibility also requires effective baseline hyperparameters, remaining compute allocations and a policy for incomplete four-category training.

Matching initial baseline tensors does not preserve subsequent random sampling and dropout: constructing nn.Linear consumes random draws before its weights are overwritten. Preserve the training RNG stream when attaching the gate.

Execution failures remain unresolved. Establish forward and gradient agreement with retention fixed at one before interpreting architectural changes; zero score discrepancies do not explain nonzero final-feature discrepancies.

Deferring constant-retention controls prevents attribution of gains to item conditioning. Originality 3 is reasonable, potential 6 is speculative, and difficulty 4 may underestimate custom recurrent execution, throughput loss and export work. Gate diagnostics alone cannot rule out item-frequency shortcuts.
